variants.name: scene_centered
variants.prompt:
Use case: infographic-diagram.
Asset type: a polished CVPR research-paper teaser LAYOUT MOCKUP, not a presentation slide, not real experimental results.
Create ONE wide landscape raster figure, aspect ratio 3:1, white background, tightly composed, print-quality details. All lettering uses Times New Roman or a close elegant academic serif. Body labels clearly readable at paper width, restrained title size, no enormous headlines. Neutral charcoal for Baseline, royal blue #0057FF for Ours, muted amber for geometry callouts. Hairline rules, exact alignment, minimal dead space. Do not use rounded module boxes or a box-and-arrow pipeline.
Shared fictional scene: realistic 3D Gaussian reconstruction of an indoor robotics study room, white walls, pale wood workbench, a small printed calibration poster above it, thin black chair legs, shelves and a teal storage box. Photorealistic textured RGB regions and finely shaded dense Gaussian ellipsoids, plausible incomplete room boundaries. This is the SAME imaginary scene across all panels within the figure. Camera poses and viewpoints must be consistent. Tiny flattened ellipsoids convey surfaces, not giant beans or generic point-cloud noise. No people.
Scientific story: streaming observations of a region may be brief/intermittent. Limited training should yield fast PHOTOMETRIC convergence AND geometrically consistent maps. Do not assert faster geometric convergence, guaranteed real-time, or floater-free reconstruction. Comparisons are invented only to study future figure layout.
Mandatory small readable footer across bottom: "AI-GENERATED LAYOUT MOCKUP — NOT EXPERIMENTAL RESULTS".
No numerical metric values, no PSNR scores, no seconds, no numerical tick labels, no speedup factors. Any plot must visibly say "Schematic". No fake source citations or conference logos.

Composition A: SCENE-CENTERED evidence, three balanced zones across one continuous white canvas. Small top title "A · Scene-centered evidence".
LEFT 40%: a dominant, richly detailed oblique cutaway Gaussian room reconstruction labeled "Online map". Draw a short meaningful blue camera trajectory with four small camera frusta inside the room looking toward the workbench. Mark two compact ROI rectangles at the calibration poster and the chair/wall interface. These are the spatial origins of zooms, not workflow nodes.
MIDDLE 35%: two rows of paired equally framed crops. Column labels "Baseline" and "Ours". Upper row "Appearance detail": identical poster/workbench crop, baseline visibly softly smeared small print and shelf edge, ours crisp textured edges. Lower row "Geometry detail": identical shaded-Gaussian surface crop at chair/wall, baseline has a few spurious semitransparent splats in front of wall, ours has cleaner surface arrangement. Connect each map ROI to its corresponding crop row with thin unobtrusive leader lines; no crossing through images or labels. Use compact trapezoidal zoom connectors where useful. The same objects must persist in paired crops.
RIGHT 25%: a carefully typeset compact schematic convergence plot. Vertical label "Held-out quality", horizontal label "Completed training work", plot heading "Schematic". Gray Baseline curve rises slowly; blue Ours rises earlier then plateaus, no numbers. A single vertical dotted checkpoint intersects both curves at same training work; legend readable; label under plot "Matched training work". The dotted checkpoint indicates the illustrated map/crop comparison. Plot is subordinate to map.
Main reading order is spatial scene -> appearance and geometry evidence -> convergence. Crisp editorial research-figure design, not a generic infographic.

Composition B: MATCHED-BUDGET WHOLE-MAP COMPARISON. Small top title "B · Matched training work".
LEFT 38% and MIDDLE 38%: two dominant large maps of EXACTLY THE SAME fictional room at exactly identical elevated oblique viewing angle, zoom, illumination, crop, and online observation checkpoint. Labels "Baseline" and "Ours". Each map is split by a clean diagonal seam: upper-left region RGB textured reconstruction, lower-right region shaded dense Gaussian surface visualization. The split occurs in the same image location in both maps. Baseline RGB has some blur and incomplete thin details; baseline geometry has a few visibly misplaced splats in free space. Ours RGB has clearer poster texture and shelf edges; ours geometry clearer chair legs and wall surfaces. Both are realistic reconstruction visualizations, not perfectly polished CAD meshes.
Below each map, one wide modest-height inset of the SAME selected poster/workbench ROI. Thin amber dashed ROI outline on each map and precise trapezoid zoom leaders attach it to its inset. Align map and inset across both methods. Small labels "RGB / Gaussian geometry" and "Appearance detail" used once clearly.
RIGHT 24%: compact unobtrusive plot labeled "Schematic", vertical axis "Held-out quality", horizontal axis "Completed training work". Gray Baseline and blue Ours, ours improves earlier. No numerical labels. A single dotted vertical line gives equal work, with readable label "Same budget". 
Map pair dominates visual area; plot is narrower supporting evidence. This must look clearly different from a single hero map with a grid of detail witnesses. No full GT column. Tight academic layout.

variants.prompt:

Composition C: BRIEF OBSERVATION AND PROGRESSION. Small top title "C · Brief observations, continued refinement".
LEFT 26%: a compact but detailed oblique cutaway Gaussian room map with a small blue camera trajectory. Highlight the workbench/poster as ONE target region with an amber rectangle. Show two camera frusta looking at the target then a later frustum pointing away. Label "Target region". Beneath map, a slim four-thumbnail incoming RGB strip follows camera motion: target visible in first two thumbnails, third turning away, fourth elsewhere. Thin time arrow beneath, two short annotations "Briefly observed" and "Stream continues". Do not depict all data available beforehand. One thin leader connects target ROI to the comparison block.
CENTER 50%: a precisely aligned two-column, two-row comparison grid. Columns "After observation" and "Later in the stream". Rows "Baseline" (charcoal) and "Ours" (blue). All FOUR images render the EXACT SAME held-out viewpoint of the marked poster/workbench region, NOT the current incoming camera view. Baseline early blurred, baseline later somewhat improved but still smeared poster texture. Ours early recognizable, ours later clear detail. Keep the same room contents, colors, perspective and crop across all four. Small line underneath: "Same evaluation view · matched checkpoints". No numbers, no artificial scores.
RIGHT 24%: clearly separated but aligned two vertically stacked shaded-Gaussian crops of the same target surface with labels "Baseline" and "Ours", heading "Geometry detail". Baseline shows a few erroneous splats in front of true wall; ours shows a coherent wall/shelf surface. Small caption "Later checkpoint". This is a geometric consistency witness, NOT an assertion of faster geometry convergence.
Do NOT add a convergence chart to C; temporal image progression itself is the convergence evidence. Dense but calm scientific layout with imagery as hero, not a schematic method pipeline.
